# sandboard — agent bootstrap

Plain-text guide for an operator agent bringing up a fresh sandboard board.
Human docs: /docs (Quickstart, Your first agent, Configuration).
This file is public and needs no auth.

sandboard is a board pointed at a repository. Moving a card starts a sandboxed
coding agent; pull requests come back for a human to merge. Approving in sandboard
shows the PR; you merge on GitHub.

Work the product path. Do not invent a parallel bootstrap (extra secret stores
for values the UI already walks, host discovery of credentials, skipping
Settings). Board Settings are the source of truth; upload configuration through
the API the same way a human pastes into the UI.

## Rules that keep you out of trouble

- Every step has a check. Do not continue until it passes.
- In this stack, half-finished setup fails as a hang, not a loud error. Treat
  silence as failure.
- sandboard does not read the host keychain or OpenShell files on disk. You (or the
  human) supply PEMs and secrets over the API; the board seals them.
- `/mcp` is for operators (Projects, create_task, triage, dispatch, park,
  steer, approve). Worker verbs (`claim`, `heartbeat`, `report`, …) are
  supervisor-only.
- Dispatch spends real money and opens PRs. Confirm with the human before the
  first Project loop.

## Base URL

Use the origin you open the board on (Host / `window.location.origin`).

- UI + API + MCP share that origin (`{origin}/mcp`).
- OpenShell gateway is separate (configured in Settings → Connectivity).

## Auth

Until an admin exists, the API refuses everything except bootstrap and a few
public paths (this file, `/healthz`, `/auth/*`, MCP OAuth discovery).

1. `GET /auth/status` — if `bootstrap` is true, create admin:
   `POST /auth/bootstrap` with JSON `{ "username", "password" }`
   (password ≥ 8 chars). Returns a session cookie.
2. After bootstrap: session cookie (`sandboard_session`) or HTTP Basic with the
   local admin username/password on `/api/*`.
3. MCP: Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`. Authenticate with MCP OAuth (browser login /
   consent) once admin exists. Tokens survive sandboard restarts.

Check: `GET /api/board` returns JSON (not 401).

## Host prerequisites (outside sandboard)

These are not Settings fields. Confirm with the human / host tools before
pasting anything into sandboard.

| Need | Check |
|---|---|
| Container engine the gateway can reach | `docker info` (or equivalent) succeeds |
| OpenShell gateway up | `openshell status` → Connected + Authenticated |
| Sandbox image named by your spec | e.g. `quay.io/sandboard-app/sandbox-cursor:latest` built (`make sandbox` from repo root) — five seeded specs already point at one image per engine, see below |

`DOCKER_HOST` belongs to the gateway process, not to sandboard.

## Bootstrap order (Settings)

Same order as Welcome / Help → OpenShell + sandbox.

### 1. Connectivity — Settings → OpenShell → Connectivity

`PUT /api/openshell` with:

- `gateway_endpoint` — e.g. `https://127.0.0.1:17670`
- `ca_pem`, `client_cert_pem`, `client_key_pem` — full PEM text

If the OpenShell CLI on this machine already talks to the gateway, client PEMs
are commonly under `~/.config/openshell/gateways/<name>/mtls/` (`ca.crt`,
`tls.crt`, `tls.key`). Read them and upload; do not assume sandboard will find them.

Check: `GET /api/openshell/status` → `healthy: true`, `mtls.complete: true`,
`not_configured: false`.

### 2. Providers — Settings → OpenShell → Providers

Board provider list is the source of truth; Sync applies it to the gateway.

Typical fresh install for Cursor-engine boards:

**Cursor Agent**

- `POST /api/openshell/providers` with
  `{ "name": "Cursor API Key", "type": "cursor-agent",
     "credentials": { "CURSOR_API_KEY": "…" } }`
- Builtin OpenShell type `cursor` is egress-only. Use board type `cursor-agent`
  when you need `CURSOR_API_KEY`.
- `POST /api/openshell/providers/sync`

**GitHub App → sandbox `GH_TOKEN`**

Do this in the product flow — not by inventing an installation-id scavenger hunt.

1. Obtain App ID + private key PEM from the human (GitHub App settings).
2. `PUT /api/github-app` with `{ "app_id", "private_key_pem" }`.
3. Read `installations` from the response (or `GET /api/github-app`).
4. Ask the human which account/org to use if more than one; then
   `PUT /api/github-app` with `{ "installation_id": <id> }`.
5. `POST /api/github-app/sync-token` — mints `GH_TOKEN` onto the `github-app`
   provider and syncs the gateway.

Optional later: webhook secret, OAuth client id/secret (GitHub login to the
board). Not required for the first sandboxed PR.

Check: `GET /api/openshell/providers` → expected names, `gateway_reachable: true`,
`gateway_synced: true`. GitHub: `token_status.configured: true`.

### 3. Policies + Sandbox specs — Settings → OpenShell

Policies are named OpenShell YAML allow-lists. Specs reference a policy by id
(image / resources / engine / providers + `policy_id`).

`GET /api/sandbox-profiles` already has five seeded rows on any board:
`sandbox-cursor`, `sandbox-agy`, `sandbox-claude`, `sandbox-opencode`, `sandbox-hermes`, each
pointed at its own `quay.io/sandboard-app/sandbox-<engine>:latest` image and a
matching minimal Cockpit policy (`cockpit-cursor`, …) with sandboard MCP already
attached. None of them is the default — seeding never picks one, because
which engine to run is the operator's call, not sandboard's guess. Set one with
`POST /api/sandbox-profiles/{id}/default` (or the UI's **Set default**), and
point Cockpit at a different one with `POST /api/sandbox-profiles/{id}/cockpit`
(or **Use for Cockpit**) instead of building a spec from scratch — only create
a new one when none of the five fit (a different image, provider set, or
resource limits):

- `POST /api/openshell/policies` with `id` (optional), `name`, `yaml`
- `GET /api/openshell/policies` → catalog; `create_default_policy_id` is the
  seeded minimal row
- `POST /api/sandbox-profiles` with `id`, `name`, `image`, `policy_id`,
  `engine` (e.g. `cursor`), `provider_names` (attach names that exist in
  Providers — instance names, not type ids).
- `POST /api/sandbox-profiles/{id}/default`

Create-form default policy is minimal (`network_policies: {}`). Add egress the
work needs under Policies (Cursor hosts, GitHub, and for cockpit: host sandboard MCP
with `protocol: mcp`) — or start from one of the five seeded Cockpit policies
above and adapt it; do not silently assume every install wants the same
allow-list.

Attach only providers that exist. Missing attach names get pruned.

Check: `GET /api/sandbox-profiles` → `default_sandbox_profile_id` set.
Welcome readiness: Gateway/mTLS + Sandbox spec both ready.

### 4. Agent runtime (optional)

`GET` / `PUT /api/agent-runtime` — engine, concurrency, timeouts. Defaults are
fine; keep `max_concurrent` at 1 until one card has finished end to end.
Dispatch starts with the process; OpenShell + a default sandbox spec are the
practical gates.

## First Project loop

Only after Connectivity, Providers, and a default sandbox spec are ready.

1. Create a Project: `POST /api/items` with level Project, intent, and required
   `clone_repo` as `owner/name`. sandboard seeds a claimable **Initial plan** Task.
2. `POST /api/items/{id}/dispatch` on the Initial plan (confirm spend with the
   human first).
3. Card moves Backlog → Running → Review with a proposed breakdown (`plan.json`).
4. Human (or operator with approval): Approve — creates sibling Tasks. Does not merge.
5. Dispatch one Task; it opens a PR and lands in Review.
6. Human merges on GitHub; card moves to Done.

After a Project exists, add more Backlog Tasks without re-running Initial plan:
board **Create Task**, or MCP `create_task` (parent = Project id). Each Task
must name its clone target (`owner/name`) in intent/DoD (Project default is
stamped when prose omits it). Approve still only materializes proposals and
never merges.

Steer / park / answer escalation / request changes as needed. Prefer park over
halt when a run is wedged (park keeps sandbox + session).

## Useful endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/llms.txt` | This guide (no auth) |
| GET | `/healthz` | Liveness (no auth) |
| GET | `/auth/status` | Bootstrap / session |
| POST | `/auth/bootstrap` | First admin |
| POST | `/auth/login` | Session cookie |
| GET | `/api/board` | Full snapshot |
| GET/PUT | `/api/openshell` | Gateway + mTLS |
| GET | `/api/openshell/status` | Health |
| GET/POST | `/api/openshell/providers` | Provider catalog |
| POST | `/api/openshell/providers/sync` | Apply to gateway |
| GET/POST | `/api/openshell/policies` | Policies catalog |
| GET/PUT | `/api/github-app` | App credentials + installation |
| POST | `/api/github-app/sync-token` | Mint GH_TOKEN |
| GET/POST | `/api/sandbox-profiles` | Specs (`policy_id`) |
| POST | `/api/sandbox-profiles/{id}/default` | Set default |
| GET/PUT | `/api/agent-runtime` | Engine / concurrency |
| POST | `/api/items` | Create Project / Task |
| POST | `/api/items/{id}/dispatch` | Start a card |

## When stuck

- Hangs → denied egress, missing provider, bad mTLS, or wedged gateway. Fix
  readiness; do not “wait longer.”
- Podman/Docker machine stopped → infrastructure; fix the host, do not burn
  card retries.
- Empty MCP tool list → reload client after OAuth.
- Provider attach does nothing → name must match Providers exactly; Sync again.
